ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: There is a uniform magnetic field inside the dashed box in Figure A. Let the direction of the magnetic field shown in Figure A be positive, and the law by which the magnetic induction intensity changes with time is as shown in Figure B. A square uniform wire frame abcd with side length l and resistance R has one half in the magnetic field, and the magnetic-field direction is perpendicular to the plane of the wire frame. It is known that at this time the heating power of side ab of the wire frame is P. Find the magnitude of the induced current in the wire frame.
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In Figure A, multiple “×” marks are drawn inside the dashed box, indicating that there is a magnetic field perpendicular to the plane of the wire frame in this region; the square wire frame is labeled a, b, c, d, where ab is a complete side on the right, bc is the lower side, cd is the left side, da is the upper side, and the whole abcd forms a single closed loop. About one half of the wire frame is in the dashed magnetic-field region. Figure B shows that the magnetic induction intensity B changes periodically and linearly with time t, but this question has already given the heating power P of side ab, and only requires finding the magnitude of the wire-frame current. Reasoning: The stem states that the square wire frame is a “uniform wire frame”, and the total resistance is R, so the resistances of the four sides are equal, and the resistance of side ab is R_ab=R/4. The wire frame is a single closed loop, and the magnitude of the current is the same everywhere, so the current in side ab is the magnitude I of the induced current in the wire frame. By Joule's law, the heating power of side ab is P=I^2 R_ab=I^2·R/4. Solving gives I^2=4P/R, therefore I=2√(P/R). Final answer: I=2√(P/R).
